text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's democratisation process will be implemented but without succumbing to international blackmail and threats to the nation's unity and integrity, military ruler General Sani Abacha says.
- United Nations fact-finding mission on disputed Bakassi peninsula should not be seen as stumbling block to the peace efforts of Togolese President Gnassingbe Eyadema, team leader Omar Halim says.
- Toxic beans scare shoots to 400 million naira the stock value of unsold beans with Lagos wholesalers.
- Banking sector regulator Central Bank may transfer its retail banking services to newly formed Atlantic Bank expected to start operations in October.
- State-run Nigerian Telecommunications (NITEL) gives approval to eight local firms to import lease lines to ensure speedy delivery of data and voice traffic in the country.
- Energy sector regulator Energy Commission of Nigeria (ECN) plans to tap and utilise available resources in order to adequately supply energy nationwide.
